games.recap: Played by Joe in the playable app and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat on 2026-11-08 as three files: the full graded play by play, the app scorecard PDF (the Payoff Pitch Gazette, Final Edition, Sunday, November 8, 2026), and the scorecard photo. Joe ruled in chat the same day: "Use this replace Yankees vs Miami game 1," adopting this playing as the new R1-01 Game 1 under the R1-05, R1-06, and R1-10 Game 1 adoption precedents; the replaced game (New York 6, Miami 2; W Whitey Ford, L Josh Johnson, SV Goose Gossage) is preserved untouched in the Yankees records at archive/replaced/. R1-01 is a frozen series and cannot be edited by import, so the replacement was made as a guarded manual edit under Joe's ruling, with the validator's locked-game fingerprint and the pins the replaced game fed (its roll count, its seed expectation, the locked counting totals) reset under dated comments in validate_results.py. The R1-01 series entry and both club records are unchanged, the Yankees having won the replaced game as well, and the series carries no MVP, before or after. All three sources agree on every number: the linescore, the batting and pitching sums, plate appearances against batters faced for every pitcher (Miami 33 against Ford's 30 and Robertson's 3; New York 41 against Johnson's 26, Ramos's 8, Scott's 3, and Cishek's 4), and printed RBI (Miami 1 for 1, Yelich; New York 8 for 8). No seed is printed in any source, so rng_seed is 0, as in the R1-06 and R1-10 adoptions. The decisions are printed in the log: Whitey Ford takes the win (8.0 IP, 5 H, 1 R, 0 ER, 1 BB, 4 SO, 0 HR) and Josh Johnson the loss (4.2 IP, 7 H, 6 R, 6 ER, 5 BB, 5 SO, 1 HR); no save, David Robertson pitching a scoreless ninth with a seven-run lead. New York scored two in the 1st (Jeter's double, Judge's walk, Gehrig's RBI single, Mantle's bunt fielder's choice forcing Judge at third, and DiMaggio's RBI single), three in the 3rd (Gehrig and Mantle walked and DiMaggio hit a three-run home run), one in the 5th (Mantle and Rodriguez singled and Berra hit a sacrifice fly), and two in the 6th (Ruth and Gehrig walked and Mantle tripled both home). Miami's only run came in the 3rd and was unearned: Realmuto struck out on Ford's wild pitch and was thrown out at first, Castillo reached on Rodriguez's error, stole third on McKeon's graded steal call with Berra's throw sailing for a second error, and scored on Yelich's groundout. The game's only home run is DiMaggio's. Errors three: Rodriguez (E5) and Berra (E2) for New York, Ramirez (E6, Rodriguez reaching in the Bottom 3) for Miami. Hit batters none, printed 0 for both clubs on the scorecard (batter HBP 0 for every hitter and pitcher HB 0 for every pitcher), not a default. Wild pitches: Ford 1, as the log and the catching line print; passed balls none. Sacrifices: Ruth's Bottom 8 bunt is the game's only sacrifice hit (SH 1) and Berra's Bottom 5 fly the only sacrifice fly. Grounded into double plays: Judge (Bottom 2) and Sheffield (Top 6), one each. Stolen bases: Castillo's steal of third is the game's only steal; no caught stealing. Substitutes: none; all 18 starters finished. Defensive lines are booked as a defense object in the established shape, a one-game exception at Joe's express direction for this replay (he asked for the advanced stats and the defense from this game), departing from the R1-06 and R1-10 adoptions, which booked no defense object under his 2026-11-05 ruling that defensive tracking begins with Winners Round 2 and Losers Round 1 and is never backfilled for Round 1; no other Round 1 game changes, and New York's 27 putouts and 9 assists and Miami's 24 putouts and 10 assists are exactly the printed fielding tables. Graded decisions, narrated here because final_grades stays empty as in every imported game in this archive: Jack McKeon (Miami) 5 (3 paid off, 0 backfired, 2 neutral): the Top 3 steal paid off (+0.74), the Bottom 5 pitching change to Ramos was neutral (-0.03), the Bottom 6 leave-in of a fatigued Ramos paid off (+1.20), the Bottom 7 change to Scott paid off (+0.73), and the Bottom 8 change to Cishek was neutral (+0.23). Casey Stengel (New York) 1 (1 paid off): the Top 9 change to Robertson paid off (+0.73). Managers: Casey Stengel (New York) and Jack McKeon (Miami). Venue is Yankee Stadium. Availability: Game 2 is unaffected by the swap. Ford (23 outs in the replaced game, 24 here) and Johnson (18, then 14) were unavailable for Game 2 under either version and neither pitched in it, and every reliever who worked Game 2 was a free arm under both versions: Cishek threw 3 outs in each version, Alfonseca was free under the replaced game and does not appear in this one, and Robertson was free at 3 outs here and does not appear in the replaced one; Gossage's replaced-game save leaves the book with the replaced game. New York leads the series 1-0.

Played by Joe in the playable app and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat on 2026-11-08 as four files: the full graded play by play, the scorecard CSV export (line, batting, pitching, fielding, and play sections), the app scorecard PDF (the Payoff Pitch Gazette, Final Edition, Sunday, November 8, 2026), and the scorecard photo. Joe ruled in chat the same day: "Replace this with game 1 dodger vs brewers," adopting this playing as the new R1-10 Game 1 under the R1-05 Game 1 and R1-06 Game 1 adoption precedents; the replaced game (Los Angeles 6, Milwaukee 5 in 10 innings, W Eric Gagne, L Rollie Fingers, Roy Campanella's walk-off home run in the Bottom 10, booked 2026-11-01) is preserved untouched in the Dodgers records at archive/replaced/. All four sources agree on every number: the linescore, the batting and pitching sums, plate appearances against batters faced for every pitcher, and printed RBI (Milwaukee 0 for 1, its run scoring on a wild pitch; Los Angeles 11 for 12, Pee Wee Reese's Bottom 4 run scoring on Zack Wheat's single with no RBI printed in any source, booked as printed). No seed is printed in any of the four sources, so rng_seed is 0, as in the replaced game and the rest of the series. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log and the run charges. Sandy Koufax takes the win with a complete game: 9.0 IP, 3 H, 1 R, 1 ER, 3 BB, 1 HB, 9 SO, 0 HR, 34 BF. Teddy Higuera takes the loss: Los Angeles took the lead for good in the Bottom 1 on Shohei Ohtani's two-run home run, and Higuera is charged with six runs (Ohtani's homer scored Zack Wheat and Ohtani in the 1st, Ron Cey's homer scored Gil Hodges and Cey in the 4th, and Reese and Jackie Robinson, who singled off him in the 4th, scored on singles off Dan Plesac); his printed line reads 4 ER, the two Bottom 1 runs unearned as printed after Brice Turang's error. No save. Run charges match the printed lines exactly: Milwaukee pitching allows 6 + 3 + 3 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 12 (Higuera, Plesac, Fingers, Devin Williams, Jeremy Jeffress, Ken Sanders), and Los Angeles pitching allows 1 (Koufax). The game: Milwaukee scored in the Top 1, Christian Yelich singling, stealing second during Paul Molitor's hit-and-run strikeout, taking third on Robin Yount's fly out, and scoring on Koufax's wild pitch during Prince Fielder's at-bat (Koufax WP 1 as printed). Los Angeles answered in the Bottom 1: Wheat reached on Turang's error (E4) and Ohtani hit a two-run home run off Higuera. The Bottom 4 scored seven: Hodges singled, Roy Campanella bunted him to second, Cey hit a two-run home run, Reese and Robinson singled, Plesac relieved, Wheat singled home Reese, Mookie Betts singled home Robinson, and Duke Snider hit a three-run home run. The Bottom 5 scored three off Fingers: Campanella and Reese singled and Wheat hit a three-run home run. Los Angeles hit four home runs (Ohtani, Cey, Snider, Wheat) and Milwaukee none; home runs allowed split Higuera 2, Plesac 1, Fingers 1. Errors: Turang's E4 is the game's only error, and errors_by carries him as the sources print it; Los Angeles made none. Hit batter: Geoff Jenkins, hit by Koufax in the Top 7 (HB 1 for Koufax, HBP 1 for Jenkins), as printed on the card, so the hit batter check runs on real data. Wild pitches as printed: Koufax 1 and Plesac 1; a wild pitch is not a stored archive field and both are noted here only. Sacrifices: Campanella's Bottom 4 bunt is the game's only sacrifice (SH 1); no sacrifice flies. Stolen bases: Yelich's steal of second is the game's only steal; the three other steal sends (Jenkins in the Top 5, Molitor in the Top 6, Carlos Gómez in the Top 8) were held runners who did not get a good jump, not attempts, and there was no caught stealing. Double plays grounded into: none for either club; the two forceouts (Ohtani's fielder's choice in the Bottom 3 and Robinson's forceout in the Bottom 7) are not GIDPs. Substitutions: Ryan Braun pinch-hit for Yelich in the Top 6 and stayed in left field (0 for 2); Los Angeles made none, its starting nine batting the whole game. Batters faced tie to the batting PA totals both ways: Milwaukee 34 PA against Koufax's 34 BF; Los Angeles 41 PA against 41 Milwaukee BF (Higuera 19, Plesac 5, Fingers 6, Williams 4, Jeffress 4, Sanders 3). The printed fielding lines are carried in the official record; no defense object is booked, under Joe's 2026-11-05 ruling that defensive tracking begins with Winners Round 2 and Losers Round 1 and is never backfilled for Round 1. Thirteen decisions were graded, all for Pat Murphy (Milwaukee): 5 paid off, 7 backfired, 1 neutral. The Bottom 4 pitching change to Plesac backfired at -4.12 (five runs scored in the rest of the inning) and the Bottom 5 change to Fingers backfired at -2.77; the two leave-in calls on fatigued pitchers paid off at +0.35 each, and the changes to Williams (Bottom 6), Jeffress (Bottom 7), and Sanders (Bottom 8) paid off at +0.73 each as the game quieted down. Tommy Lasorda (Los Angeles) made no graded decisions. Managers: Pat Murphy (Milwaukee) and Tommy Lasorda (Los Angeles). Venue is Dodger Stadium. Game 2 availability, under the house outs convention read off this game only: Koufax threw 27 outs and Higuera 10, so both are UNAVAILABLE for Game 2 (the rotations turn to the number 2 starters anyway); Plesac (2 outs), Fingers (3), Williams (3), Jeffress (3), and Sanders (3) are all free. Eric Gagne and Kenley Jansen, who pitched in the replaced Game 1, did not pitch in this one; Game 2 stands as played, and its official record carries a dated note that its availability provenance referred to the replaced game. Los Angeles leads the series 1-0.

Played by Joe and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat as three files on 2026-11-02: the paper scorecard grid photo, the app scorecard PDF, and the full graded play-by-play text; official R1-11 Game 1 under Joe's standing rule that sending a fixture's box score makes the game count. Oakland Athletics (seed 22) vs Philadelphia Phillies (seed 11), home pattern 2-2-1-1-1, Game 1 at Citizens Bank Park in Philadelphia, and Oakland leads the series 1-0 with this win. Box score record: the three sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, and a complete play log, and they agree on every printed number, with one run-accounting settlement (the Top 8 wild pitch run, below) and no other knot. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log and the run charges on the card. Catfish Hunter takes the win: he left in the Bottom 6 with one out, runners at first and second, and a 5-3 lead, and the lead held the rest of the way (5.1 IP, 10 H, 3 ER, 0 BB, 3 SO, 2 HR). Steve Carlton takes the loss: he was charged with eight runs in 7.1 innings (10 H, 8 ER, 5 BB, 6 SO, 2 HR), five of them his own runners and three of them runners he left behind who scored behind Brad Lidge in the Top 8 (Steinbach on the wild pitch, Ellis on Chavez's double, and Murphy, who scored on Ellis's single off Carlton himself). No save: Dennis Eckersley closed the Bottom 9 with a six-run lead, 11-5, so no save arises. Run charges match the printed lines exactly: Philadelphia pitching allows 8 + 3 + 0 = 11 (Carlton eight, Lidge three, Papelbon none), and Oakland pitching allows 3 + 1 + 1 + 0 = 5 (Hunter three, Doolittle one, Hendriks one, Eckersley none). The charge detail: Carlton's eight are Murphy's Top 2 solo home run, four in the Top 5 (Henderson walked and scored on Jackson's single, Bando and Jackson singled and scored with McGwire on McGwire's 3-run home run), Murphy again in the Top 8 (walked and scored on Ellis's single, Carlton's last batter), Steinbach in the Top 8 (singled off Carlton and scored on Lidge's wild pitch, so the run stays Carlton's), and Ellis in the Top 8 (singled off Carlton and scored on Chavez's double behind Lidge). Lidge's three are Henderson in the Top 8 (Lidge hit him himself, and he scored on Chavez's double) and Tejada and Steinbach in the Top 9 (both reached off Lidge and scored on Ellis's double). Hunter's three are Callison in the Bottom 1 (singled and scored on Schmidt's double), Callison again in the Bottom 3 (solo home run), and Howard in the Bottom 4 (solo home run); Doolittle's one is Klein's Bottom 7 solo home run and Hendriks's one is Rollins's Bottom 8 solo home run. Printed RBI: Oakland 10 (McGwire 3, Ellis 3, Chavez 2, Jackson 1, Murphy 1) against 11 runs, the one run without an RBI being Steinbach's Top 8 run on Lidge's wild pitch (settlement below), and Philadelphia 5 (Callison 1, Klein 1, Schmidt 1, Howard 1, Rollins 1) against 5 runs, clean. The settlement: in the Top 8, after Ellis's single made it 6-4, Lidge relieved, hit Henderson to load the bases (Steinbach at third, Ellis at second, Henderson at first), and during Chavez's pinch-hit at-bat Lidge threw a wild pitch (the card prints WP: Brad Lidge 1) that scored Steinbach and moved Ellis and Henderson up; Chavez then doubled both of them home. That is why the printed batting line gives Chavez 2 RBI and not 3, why Oakland's printed RBI total is 10 for 11 runs, and why the play log's line on the double reads three runs in the inning sequence while only two of them ride on the double. The duplicate test ran before the number was assigned: the R1-11 series entry carried no stored games, so this box score is no duplicate, and this is the first game of the series in play order, booked as Game 1. The game: Philadelphia scored first in the Bottom 1 (Callison singled, Abreu moved him over, and Schmidt doubled him home), Murphy's solo home run tied it in the Top 2, and solo home runs by Callison in the Bottom 3 and Howard in the Bottom 4 put Philadelphia up 3-1. Oakland's Top 5 turned the game: Steinbach and Ellis went quietly, Henderson walked, Bando and Jackson singled (Jackson's drove Henderson home), and McGwire hit a 3-run home run for a 5-3 lead. Hunter left in the Bottom 6 with the bases filling, and Doolittle walked Rollins to load them before striking out Callison and getting Abreu to line out, stranding three. Klein's home run in the Bottom 7 cut it to 5-4. The Top 8 broke it open: Tejada grounded out, Murphy walked, Steinbach and Ellis singled (Ellis's scored Murphy, the last batter Carlton faced), Lidge came in and hit Henderson, threw the wild pitch that scored Steinbach, and gave up Chavez's two-run double for a 9-4 lead. Rollins homered in the Bottom 8 to make it 9-5. In the Top 9, Canseco struck out, Tejada singled, Murphy flied out, Steinbach walked, and Ellis doubled both runners home off Lidge; Papelbon struck out Henderson to end the inning at 11-5. Eckersley pitched a scoreless Bottom 9 (Klein singled and stole second behind him, stranded at third). Philadelphia out-hit Oakland 14 to 13 and stranded 10 runners, including the bases loaded in the Bottom 6. Home runs: Oakland two (Murphy, McGwire) and Philadelphia four (Callison, Howard, Klein, Rollins). Doubles: Ellis and Chavez for Oakland and Schmidt and Howard for Philadelphia; no triples. Errors: none by either club. Hit batters: one, Henderson, hit by Lidge in the Top 8 (the card prints HBP by: Brad Lidge 1); the scorecard grids print an HBP column for every pitcher on both clubs, so HB is carried card-sourced for all seven pitchers (Lidge 1, the other six 0) and the hit batter check runs on real data. Wild pitch: Lidge 1, printed, the Top 8 run described above. Sacrifices: Schmidt's Bottom 3 sacrifice bunt is the game's only sacrifice of either kind, so the split lines read SH 1 for Schmidt and SH 0 and SF 0 for every other batter, log-proven. Stolen bases, as printed: Klein 2 (Bottom 3 and Bottom 9); Manuel's other graded steal send in the Bottom 9 was a held runner who did not get a good jump, not an attempt. Caught stealing: none. Double plays grounded into, counted from the play log: one, Ellis in the Top 6 (a 3-4-3 double play that erased the threat after the Murphy and Steinbach singles). Substitutions: Oakland made one, Eric Chavez pinch-hit for Sal Bando in the Top 8 and stayed in at third base, doubling home two runs (1 for 1); Bando himself had walked in the Top 7, before the change. Philadelphia made no substitution of any kind. Batters faced are counted from the play log and tie to the batting PA totals both ways (Oakland 46 PA against 46 Philadelphia BF: Carlton 36, Lidge 9, Papelbon 1; Philadelphia 42 PA against 42 Oakland BF: Hunter 26, Doolittle 7, Hendriks 5, Eckersley 4). Oakland PA is AB 39 plus BB 6 plus Henderson's hit by pitch; Philadelphia PA is AB 40 plus BB 1 plus Schmidt's sacrifice bunt. Nine decisions were graded. Dick Williams made 4 (2 paid off, 0 backfired, 2 neutral): the Bottom 6 pitching change to Sean Doolittle paid off at +0.63, the game's signature call, walking the bases loaded and then escaping with no runs; the Top 8 pinch hitter Chavez paid off at +1.71, the game's best single grade; the Bottom 8 pitching change to Liam Hendriks was neutral at -0.27 (Rollins homered behind it) and the Bottom 9 change to Dennis Eckersley neutral at +0.23. Charlie Manuel made 5 (1 paid off, 2 backfired, 2 neutral): the Top 9 pitching change to Jonathan Papelbon paid off at +0.57; the Top 8 pitching change to Brad Lidge backfired at -2.37, the game's worst single grade (hit batter, wild pitch run, and a two-run double behind it); the Bottom 9 steal send backfired at -0.86 (Klein held); and two steal sends were neutral at -0.26 each (Bottom 3 and Bottom 9, Klein safe both times). Managers: Dick Williams (Oakland) and Charlie Manuel (Philadelphia). Venue is Citizens Bank Park. Game 2 availability, under the house convention that reads only this game: Hunter (16 outs) and Carlton (22 outs) are both UNAVAILABLE, and Doolittle (5 outs), Lidge (4), Hendriks (3), Eckersley (3) and Papelbon (1) are all free. Both clubs started their rotation number 1, Hunter for Oakland and Carlton for Philadelphia, and the rotations turn to the number 2 starters for Game 2 regardless.

Played by Joe and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat as three files on 2026-11-02: the paper scorecard grid photo, the app scorecard PDF, and the full graded play-by-play text; official R1-11 Game 2 under Joe's standing rule that sending a fixture's box score makes the game count. Oakland Athletics (seed 22) vs Philadelphia Phillies (seed 11), home pattern 2-2-1-1-1, Game 2 at Citizens Bank Park in Philadelphia, and Oakland leads the series 2-0 with this win. Box score record: the three sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, and a complete play log, and they agree on every printed number, with the run-accounting settlements below and no other knot. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log and the run charges on the card. Andrew Bailey takes the win, a scorer's choice: starter Vida Blue pitched only 4.0 innings and faced one batter in the Bottom 5, Klein, whose leadoff home run was Blue's sixth run charged, so at under five innings Blue cannot take the win; Liam Hendriks relieved and recorded no outs, allowing Schmidt's single and Harper's 2-run home run; Bailey then retired Howard, Utley and Ruiz in order, two of them on strikes, for a scoreless Bottom 5 with Oakland ahead 13-8, and the lead never changed hands again (Oakland led from the Top 1 onward and Philadelphia never tied it after the Top 5). Robin Roberts takes the loss: the runs that put Oakland ahead to stay came off him in the Top 1, Philadelphia trailed 6-5 when his work ended after the Top 4, and the Phillies never tied or led again, even though Ranger Suarez gave up the seven-run Top 5 behind him. No save: Dennis Eckersley closed the Bottom 9 with a four-run lead, 15-11. Run charges match the printed lines exactly: Philadelphia pitching allows 6 + 7 + 0 + 1 + 1 = 15 (Roberts six, Suarez seven, Reed none, Lidge one, Papelbon one), and Oakland pitching allows 6 + 2 + 0 + 0 + 2 + 1 + 0 = 11 (Blue six, Hendriks two, Bailey none, Doolittle none, Fingers two, Honeycutt one, Eckersley none). The charge detail: Roberts's six are the three in the Top 1 (Henderson unearned, below; Bando and Canseco earned on Canseco's 2-run home run), Canseco again in the Top 3 (doubled and scored on Tejada's single), and two unearned runs in the Top 4 (Henderson on Rollins's error, below; Bando, who scored on McGwire's single after the error should have ended the inning), which is why his printed line reads 6 R and only 3 ER. Suarez's seven are the entire seven-run Top 5, every run charged to him: Canseco (walked, scored on Steinbach's single), Tejada (singled, scored on Ellis's single), Steinbach and Ellis (singled, scored on Jackson's single), and Henderson, Jackson and McGwire on McGwire's 3-run home run. Lidge's one is Canseco in the Top 8 (doubled, scored on Murphy's single) and Papelbon's one is Chavez's Top 9 pinch-hit home run. Blue's six are the five in the Bottom 4 (Schmidt on Utley's double, Howard and Utley on Rollins's single, Rollins and Callison on Callison's 2-run home run) and Klein's Bottom 5 leadoff home run, the one batter Blue faced in the fifth. Hendriks's two are Schmidt and Harper in the Bottom 5 (singled, then scored with Harper on Harper's 2-run home run). Fingers's two are Schmidt and Harper in the Bottom 7, Schmidt unearned (below) and Harper earned on his second home run. Honeycutt's one is Ruiz in the Bottom 8. Printed RBI: Oakland 13 (McGwire 4, Canseco 2, Jackson 2, Tejada 1, Murphy 1, Steinbach 1, Ellis 1, Chavez 1) against 15 runs, the two runs without an RBI both being Henderson's error runs, settled below; and Philadelphia 10 (Harper 4, Callison 2, Rollins 2, Klein 1, Utley 1) against 11 runs, the one run without an RBI being Ruiz's Bottom 8 run, settled below. The settlements: in the Top 1, Henderson singled and stole second, and Bando's single plus Schmidt's error at third (batter to second) scored him; the scorer charged no RBI on the play, so Henderson's run is unearned and carries no RBI, while the two runs on Canseco's home run behind it are earned. In the Top 4, Steinbach walked, Ellis flied out, and Henderson forced Steinbach at second; Bando singled Henderson to third, Jackson reached on Rollins's error at short and Henderson scored on the play (unearned, no RBI), and McGwire's single scored Bando (unearned, coming after what should have been the third out). In the Bottom 7, Schmidt reached on Chavez's 2-base error at third and scored on Harper's home run: the run is unearned on Fingers's line but carries Harper's RBI, as a home run run does. In the Bottom 8, Ruiz doubled, Rollins bunted him to third, and he scored on Honeycutt's wild pitch during Callison's strikeout (the card prints WP: Rick Honeycutt 1), which is why Philadelphia's printed RBI total is 10 for 11 runs. The duplicate test ran before the number was assigned: the stored R1-11 Game 1 (Oakland 11, Philadelphia 5) shares neither this game's final score nor its linescore, so this box score is no duplicate, and this is the second game of the series in play order, booked as Game 2. The game: Oakland scored three in the Top 1 on Henderson's single and steal, Bando's single plus error, and Canseco's 2-run home run. Canseco doubled and Tejada singled him home in the Top 3, and the two unearned Top 4 runs made it 6-0. Philadelphia's five-run Bottom 4 off Blue answered: Schmidt walked, Howard singled, Utley doubled Schmidt home, Rollins singled Howard and Utley home, and Callison hit a 2-run home run to cut it to 6-5. Oakland blew it open with seven in the Top 5 off Suarez, on five singles and McGwire's 3-run home run, before Reed came in and shut Oakland down for 2.1 innings. Philadelphia kept hitting: Klein's solo home run off Blue leading off the Bottom 5, Harper's 2-run home run off Hendriks in the same inning (Bailey then stopped it cold), and Harper's second 2-run home run off Fingers in the Bottom 7 after Schmidt reached on Chavez's error, cutting it to 13-10. Canseco doubled and Murphy singled him home off Lidge in the Top 8; Ruiz doubled, took third on Rollins's bunt, and scored on Honeycutt's wild pitch in the Bottom 8; and Chavez, who had pinch-hit in the Top 7 and struck out, hit a solo home run off Papelbon in the Top 9 for the final margin. Eckersley pitched a perfect Bottom 9. Home runs: Oakland three (Canseco, McGwire, Chavez) and Philadelphia four (Callison, Klein, Harper two). Doubles: Canseco two for Oakland and Utley and Ruiz for Philadelphia; no triples. Errors: Philadelphia two (Schmidt in the Top 1, Rollins in the Top 4) and Oakland one (Chavez in the Bottom 7). Hit batters: none; the scorecard grids print an HBP column for every pitcher on both clubs and it reads zero for all twelve, so HB 0 is carried for every pitcher as card-sourced values and the hit batter check runs on real data. Wild pitches, as printed: Blue 1, Honeycutt 1 (the Bottom 8 run described above), and Lidge 1. Sacrifices: Rollins's Bottom 8 bunt is the game's only sacrifice of either kind, so the split lines read SH 1 for Rollins and SH 0 and SF 0 for every other batter, log-proven. Stolen bases, as printed: Henderson (Top 1). Caught stealing: Henderson (Top 7). Double plays grounded into, counted from the play log: one, Abreu in the Bottom 6 (a 4-6-3 double play behind Doolittle). Substitutions: Oakland made one, Eric Chavez pinch-hit for Sal Bando in the Top 7, stayed in at third base, struck out in the seventh and homered in the ninth (1 for 2); Bando's own line carries his Top 1 and Top 4 singles. Philadelphia made no substitution of any kind.
